newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium calls on Zaire and Rwanda for restraint.
newsitem.headline: Belgium calls on Zaire and Rwanda for restraint.

text.p: Belgium called on Saturday for restraint from both Zaire and Rwanda in their raging border conflict and urged the warring parties to do all in their power to let refugees in Zaire return home to Rwanda.

A two-week lightning offensive in eastern Zaire by Tutsi rebels, some backed by Rwandan government forces, has thrown Zaire's army into disarray and left more than a million Rwandan Hutu refugees trapped and at high risk.
Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke warned Rwanda in a statement against "all military incursions into Zairean territory, the integrity of which can in no way be violated."

At the same time he urged Zairean armed forces to "abstain from all provocation". Belgium is the former colonial power of the sprawling central African country, while its smaller neighbours Rwanda and Burundi were once Belgian protectorates.

Stepping up Belgium's diplomatic efforts, Derycke said he was sending a high-level mission to the Zairean capital Kinshasa this weekend and that he and Belgium's Secretary of State for Cooperation and Development Reginald Moreels would meet Rwanda's Foreign Minister Anastase Gasana on Monday in Brussels.
The statement was issued through Belgian news agency Belga.

The refugees, who fled Rwanda and neighbouring Burundi after Tutsi rivals took control of their own countries, presented a destabilising influence in the region, Derycke said. He said safe corridors should be created to help them get home.
The refugees were left to fend for themselves on Saturday as the last aid workers fled for their lives.
Following a request by Derycke and Moreels, European Union ministers are due to meet in Brussels next Thursday to discuss emergency humanitarian support in the Zairean crisis.
